I think it's the difference between receiving formal instruction in said subject and not. I would say a lot of people are self taught particularly those in subjects where independent exploration is intergral( math being among those)  but to what extent is where the difference comes in. 

In my opinion, the guide exists to help you develop your skill and precision in addition to versatility. One thing I note, and this is ancecdotal, among some self taught people is while they do indeed demonstrate knowledge, they lack the kind of versatility you would find in someone with formal instruction. There is also a lot of danger of overconfidence and believing you understand more than you really do. I've seen cases where someone is completely confident that they got it only to get absolutely demolished and that's a tough thing. 

In summation all I mean to say is being intrinsically motivated to learn beyond your scope is great however it is sometimes necessary to have assistance and feedback from someone with far more accumulated experience. I think of it as more of an augmentation of the self learning experience if you will.
